The Depression Acoustic Encoder suppresses speaker identity and linguistic information through adversarial objectives, using a gradient reversal layer (GRL) to discourage speaker-specific information in the shared embedding [c2]. Additionally, a linguistic-adversarial branch reduces residual phonetic content in the depression embedding [c2].
The Depression Acoustic Encoder (DAE) achieved a robust ROC-AUC of 0.693 in linear probing, proving that severity information is preserved even as speaker and content are suppressed [c8].

The DAIC-WOZ dataset exhibits strong coupling between linguistic sentiment and diagnostic labels, suggesting that models trained on this data are naturally encouraged to rely on sentiment cues rather than depression-related acoustic markers. This is because negative sentiment is substantially more frequent in depressed than in healthy speech, indicating that linguistic sentiment is not independent of depression status [c4].

This approach allows for single-pass retrieval, avoiding per-query LLM calls, which are costly, latency-sensitive, and operationally brittle [c5].

ADAR simulates a continuous process of gradual degradation of positive samples through a diffusion process, where a positive sample progressively loses its informative characteristics and eventually becomes indistinguishable from a negative sample [c8].
ADAR improves AHNS by 3.13% in Recall@10 on Amazon-Beauty [c1].

ADAR generates negative samples instead of drawing them from the item pool because existing methods tend to mis-label potentially positive but unobserved items as negatives and lack precise control over negative sample selection. [c9]

The framework analyzed passenger feedback from TripAdvisor, a platform where passengers can leave unstructured reviews about their experiences with airlines, including EgyptAir and Emirates [c5].

The severity variable measures the impact level of an accident on traffic, quantified on a scale of 1 to 4, with 1 representing the least impact and 4 representing the greatest impact, based on traffic delay duration [41].
The representative sample contains 500,000 entries from the complete dataset of over 7.7 million traffic accident records [c2].

Precipitation and visibility showed limited predictive power for accident severity because they were highly localized and did not exhibit a clear relationship with severity, with precipitation and visibility densities primarily located at high values without apparent relationship to severity, and visibility densities were primarily located at high values without illuminating severity relationships [c2, c4].
The Weighted XGBoost classifier is trained for accident-severity prediction, achieving an overall accuracy of 78.2% with distinct performance characteristics across severity levels [c8].
SHAP concentration measures the mean absolute SHAP value of the top-ranked feature computed on validation data using TreeExplainer [c3].
SHAP concentration showed a Spearman correlation of ρ = 0.853 with conformal failure severity across 16 tasks [c4].

Standard distributional shift detectors fail to distinguish catastrophic from robust outcomes, and cannot predict failure severity because they detect shift uniformly across tasks but cannot capture the interaction between the model's learned dependence structure and the specific features that shift [c7].

The 40% threshold transfers to the nine non-supply-chain datasets without tuning, yielding 7/9 deterministic or near-deterministic outcomes, with Covertype correctly flagged as catastrophic and Gas Sensor correctly unflagged as robust [c6].

The active sampling strategy described in the text prioritizes uncertain states to improve exploration by sampling sub-trajectory reset points from an action-variance distribution, which is computed by aggregating the diagonal covariance of the action distribution [c1]. This strategy is inspired by classical active learning and has been shown to lead to faster and more stable convergence [c6].
The Sequential RC architecture decomposes a large reservoir into a series of smaller, interconnected reservoirs [c8].
Sequential RC maintains forecasts even at later time steps than LSTM and RNN, with no specific time difference given, but RC starts losing fine structure by t + 50, while LSTM diverges around t + 30.

Sequential RC reduces memory and computation by decomposing a large reservoir into a series of smaller, interconnected reservoirs, which allows for more efficient memory allocation and reduces the computational burden [c5]. This design enables the model to capture multi-scale temporal features without the computational overhead of backpropagation-based recurrent models [c9].
The Lorenz63 system is used to evaluate Sequential RC, a chaotic system comprising three coupled nonlinear differential equations [c3].
The FIB-4 score is calculated using age, platelet count, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) [c1].
The final one-year prediction cohort included 54,365 patients. [c10]

Serum-based fibrosis indices, such as FIB-4 and APRI, miss many advanced fibrosis cases because they rely on a limited set of laboratory parameters and do not account for sophisticated nonlinear associations or the wider set of demographics, biochemical, and clinical variables that contribute to disease progression [c5].
The XGBoost models used Bayesian hyperparameter tuning with Optuna, a hyperparameter optimization framework introduced by Akiba et al. [c3].

The reinforcement-learning agent allocates per-dimension repetition counts based on semantic importance, dynamically adjusting the allocation to minimize semantic distortion [c10]. The allocation is done via a learned policyπθ that assigns per-dimension repetition counts t to quantized embeddings, optimized to minimize semantic distortion DS under a fixed channel-use budget B [c3].
The framework achieves a 0.3123 (0.2710–0.3498) improvement in chrF score over uniform protection at 1 dB SNR [c8].

The framework uses repetition coding because it provides a tractable action space for a reinforcement learning agent tasked with per-dimension allocation, and its decoding mechanism is computationally trivial and can be parallelized across dimensions [c5].
The AG News dataset is used for the comprehensive evaluation of the proposed framework [c6].
The SSI-GAN stands for Semi-supervised Swin-Inspired Generative Adversarial Network [c9].
SSI-GAN reached 99.93% classification accuracy on the third day post-infection with only 3% labeled data [c4].

SSI-GAN uses semi-supervised adversarial learning to leverage large amounts of unlabeled spike data, reducing the dependency on expensive and labor-intensive manual labeling, and maintaining high classification accuracy [c3].
The Optuna platform is used to optimize the hyperparameters of the SSI-GAN model, employing Bayesian methods to find the best configuration [c1].
The latent-constrained CVAE enforces cross-realization homogeneity of latent embeddings at a small set of shared geographic "anchor" locations [c4].
The dataset consists of output from the ERA5 reanalysis model, providing 10 independent realizations of 2 monthly averaged mean surface temperature from 1940 to the present [c2].

A jointly trained vanilla CVAE fails to generalize to unseen ensemble members because it yields a fragmented latent space, where each realization occupies its own subspace with no discernible alignment across realizations, despite the known correspondence in geographic space [c3].
We employ multi-output Gaussian process regression (GPR) to predict latent coordinates at unseen locations in an unseen realization, trained via sparse variational inference [c5].
